questions.q: The prototypes printed for axonal neuropathy and demyelinating radiculoneuropathy are:
questions.exp: Features table prototypes: Axonal Neuropathy (prototype : DM); Demyelinating radiculoneuropathy prototype : GBS (Book p624)

questions.q: A 58-year-old diabetic develops symmetrical distal sensory-motor loss evolving over many months. Which onset pattern and exception does the book attach to this axonal prototype?
questions.exp: Axonal: usually gradual and insidious onset, Exception : Porphyria (Acute) (Book p624)

questions.q: Onset of demyelinating radiculoneuropathy is usually:
questions.exp: Demyelinating: usually acute or subacute, Exception : CIDP (Chronic) (Book p624)

questions.q: Which fibres and distribution are affected early in axonal neuropathy?
opts: Large and long axons early, hence initially lower extremities; small fibres
Large fibers diffusely, not always distal
questions.exp: Axonal: large and long axons affected early, hence initially lower extremities; small fibres (Book p624)

questions.q: The demyelinating process is described as:
opts: Diffuse, starts in lower limbs but not always distal; large fibers
questions.exp: Demyelinating: diffuse process, starts in lower limbs but not always distal; large fibers (Book p624)

questions.q: Stocking-glove sensory-motor loss with symmetrical distal signs in legs and arms characterises:
questions.exp: Axonal: stocking-glove sensory-motor loss results in symmetrical distal clinical signs in the legs and arms (Book p624)

questions.q: Generalized weakness with mild sensory loss characterises:
questions.exp: Demyelinating: generalized weakness and mild sensory loss (Book p624)

questions.q: Involvement pattern in axonal vs demyelinating disease is:
opts: Distal in axonal; proximal and distal in demyelinating
Proximal in axonal; distal in demyelinating
questions.exp: Axonal distal involvement; demyelinating proximal and distal involvement (Book p624)

questions.q: In that slowly progressive diabetic neuropathy, which reflex pattern does the table predict?
opts: Ankle jerk lost early with proximal tendon reflexes preserved
questions.exp: Axonal: ankle jerk lost early and proximal tendon reflexes preserved (Book p624)

questions.q: Areflexia with all reflexes lost early characterises:
questions.exp: Demyelinating: all reflexes are lost early (Areflexia) (Book p624)

questions.q: A chronic neuropathy patient shows prominent muscle wasting on examination. Which column of the table does this favour?
opts: Common in demyelinating and absent in axonal
Common in axonal and relatively absent in demyelinating
questions.exp: Muscle wasting common (axonal) vs relatively absent (demyelinating) (Book p624)

questions.q: CSF proteins in axonal vs demyelinating disease are:
opts: Normal in axonal as only axons are involved; elevated in demyelinating since nerve roots are involved
Elevated in axonal; normal in demyelinating
questions.exp: CSF proteins normal as only axons are involved vs elevated since nerve roots are involved (Book p624)

questions.q: Recovery and residual deformity in axonal vs demyelinating disease are:
opts: Slow recovery with residual deformity common in axonal; rapid recovery with residual deformity less common in demyelinating
Rapid recovery in axonal; slow recovery in demyelinating
questions.exp: Axonal slow recovery, residual deformity common; demyelinating rapid recovery, residual deformity less common (Book p624)

questions.q: Nerve conduction in axonal vs demyelinating disease is:
opts: Normal or slightly lowered in axonal; slowed in demyelinating
Slowed in axonal; normal in demyelinating
questions.exp: Nerve conduction normal or slightly lowered vs nerve conduction is slowed (Book p624)

questions.q: Acute demyelinating radiculoneuropathies listed are:
opts: AIDP (<4 weeks), diphtheria, and drugs amiodarone, chloroquine, gold
questions.exp: Acute: AIDP <4 weeks; Diphtheria; Drugs Amiodarone, Chloroquine, Gold (Book p624)

questions.q: Chronic demyelinating radiculoneuropathies listed are:
opts: CIDP (>8 weeks), POEMS, myeloma, HIV and CTS (mononeuropathy)
questions.exp: Chronic: CIDP >8 weeks; POEMS; Myeloma; HIV; CTS (Carpal Tunnel Syndrome) - mononeuropathy (Book p624)

questions.q: Inherited demyelinating radiculoneuropathies listed are:

questions.exp: Inherited: CMTD (Charcot Marie Tooth Disease); Refsum's disease (Book p624)

units.title: 1. Radiculopathies: Axonal vs Demyelinating Features and Causes
units.guide:
Axonal neuropathy (prototype DM) is gradual and insidious except porphyria; demyelinating radiculoneuropathy (prototype GBS) is acute or subacute except CIDP.
Axonal disease hits large long axons early with stocking-glove distal signs, ankle jerk lost early, wasting, normal CSF proteins, slow recovery and residual deformity; demyelinating disease is diffuse with generalized weakness, areflexia, raised CSF proteins, rapid recovery and slowed conduction.
Demyelinating causes split into acute (AIDP <4 weeks, diphtheria, drugs amiodarone/chloroquine/gold), chronic (CIDP >8 weeks, POEMS, myeloma, HIV, CTS) and inherited (CMTD, Refsum's).

units.title: 2. Notes, ANS Predominant Neuropathies and Patterns of LMN Lesions
units.sec: Neuropathy Notes, ANS Predominant & LMN Patterns
units.guide:
Pure sensory neuropathy is ganglionopathy; pure motor neuropathies are lead, dapsone and MMNCB; severe pain ranks small fibre > large with Fabry's > Tangier's > HIV > vasculitis.
Relapsing neuropathies are CIDP, Refsum's and porphyria; diabetic amyotrophy is asymmetric lumbosacral plexopathy; ANS predominant neuropathies use mnemonic PAD.
The eight patterns of LMN lesions map symmetric and asymmetric, proximal and distal, sensory and motor combinations to AIDP, diabetes, radiculopathy, plexopathy, pure motor neuropathy, spinal cord, muscle/NMS and ganglion.

units.title: 3. Nerve Conduction Studies and the CMAP Trace
units.guide:
Axonal loss affects only amplitude; demyelination raises latency with prolonged distal latency, conduction block or reduced velocity, temporal dispersion and prolonged or absent F wave and H reflex.
The waveform figure annotates latency, amplitude, duration, trough and recovery on amplitude (mV) vs time (ms) axes, captioned as printed Common motor axonal potential (CMAP).
